# Introduction to R

This module introduces basic R concepts that are essential for medical data analysis.

## Variables and data types

```{r}
# Numeric variables
x <- 5
pi_val <- 3.14

# Integer values
int_value <- 2L
is.integer(int_value)

# Character strings
name <- "Alice"

# Logical values
flag <- TRUE
```

## Vectors and sequences

```{r}
# Numeric vector
ages <- c(23, 35, 28)

# Sequence
seq(1, 100, 3)
seq(1, 2, length.out = 10)
```

## Factors and categorical variables

```{r}
gender <- factor(c("Male", "Female", "Male", "Female"), levels = c("Male", "Female"))
physical_activity <- factor(sample(c(1, 2), 10, replace = TRUE), levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Yes", "No"))
```

## Data structures

```{r}
# List
green_list <- list(name = "Alice", age = 25, scores = c(90, 85, 88))

# Matrix
my_matrix <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2, ncol = 3)

# Data frame
data_frame_example <- data.frame(
  ID = 1:5,
  Name = c("Alice", "Bob", "Charlie", "David", "Eva"),
  Age = sample(20:50, 5, replace = TRUE)
)
```

## Basic functions and help

```{r}
mean(c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5))
qnorm(1 - 0.05/2)
```

Use `?function_name` in the R console to view help pages.

:::
